scenario: Durable single-phase write actions checked against a captured local lease

stages.label: explicit-claim-and-single-phase-intent
stages.explanation: One fresh write job, its one-member explicit catalog and a new lease ledger are prepared. A generation-1 claim is captured in an immutable prepared-to-ready action; show remains a read and exact prepare replay returns its fixed receipt.

stages.label: same-action-callers-share-one-recorded-effect
stages.explanation: Two ordinary execute processes are launched before collection for the same action. Both return the exact same saved result and the write reaches only ready. Separate show and execute replays preserve that result; lease history remains at one event.

stages.label: new-generation-rejects-the-old-pending-action
stages.explanation: A ready-to-linked action captures generation 1 before release. A fresh claim receives generation 2. Executing the old pending action refuses lease_changed before any phase effect; its own show remains prepared and the job stays ready.

stages.label: performed-phase-and-separate-post-observation
stages.explanation: Three generation-2 actions capture the same ready phase. One performs ready-to-linked. A second observes that exact post phase and saves expected_phase_observed with effect_performed=false; the job remains linked. The third stays pending for the later beyond-post refusal.

stages.label: finish-reply-recovery-and-own-only-history
stages.explanation: With the captured write catalog absent, the final action completes the review. Its actual reply is discarded and recovered exactly. A pending action beyond its target refuses phase_changed. After lease release, all four catalog/ledger/job/target paths are hidden: recorded action show/execute replay and pending show still read only own controls. Every path returns in finally.

stages.label: exact-inputs-and-domain-boundaries-remain-explicit
stages.explanation: Changed exact requests, malformed scalar inputs and a released claim refuse. Original write jobs and lease heads remain unchanged; blocked restore jobs stay blocked. Six action intents contain four saved observations and two pending records, while only three phase effects completed the one new review.

limits: A prepared action captures one exact existing local lease and one write phase. Every new result requires that same current active claim; original review actor and execution worker are distinct self-declared labels, not authenticated participants.
The dedicated action path holds an immutable intent and at most one immutable observation. Two callers executing the same action return one saved result, while only one bounded phase is reached.

A different prepared action may find its exact expected post phase. It records expected_phase_observed with effect_performed=false and never advances to the following phase or claims causal authorship.

A pending action with stale generation refuses lease_changed; a pending action beyond its target refuses phase_changed. Its own historical show remains prepared and does not describe the current job as pending.

A real final-action reply is discarded and recovered exactly after its result is saved. No interruption, partial result, power loss, expiry wait, clock regression or unsupported bootstrap repair is demonstrated.

Completion runs with the captured catalog absent. Once a result is saved, historical show/execute replay needs only the action's own controls, even after lease release and while four catalog/ledger/job/target paths are absent. All paths return in finally.

The new wrapper checks a lease immediately before its local effect under local locks. The old direct write API and other ledgers remain outside this guard, and SQLite assignment history and filesystem effect/result do not form a common transaction.

The driver reads public API responses and lstat metadata, never private intents/results, lease SQL rows or staging contents. Original control metadata is captured after opening initial Store observations. New actions do not renew leases; metadata observations compare both jobs and earlier ledgers without changing them.
The old source/live histories remain R4/36 and R5/59 with previous quarantine, origin and blocked restore cases. New controls do not grant domain authority, deletion or archival permission.

The count of launched processes or matching saved observations does not measure maximum useful agents, simultaneous execution, model independence, semantic quality or correctness of arbitrary proposed code.
